Subject: Retention floor & redaction approach for PHI (summary + ask)

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks again for yesterday's call. MediSys is finalizing internal controls for our pilot and we need two quick confirmations to move forward with procurement:

1) Can Redwood enforce a per-tenant maximum retention window (e.g., 30/90/365 days) that is configurable by account and locked by contract? We need to know what the minimum possible retention floor is for PII/PHI and how quickly records can be purged after a request.

2) For records that must be retained for audit, what redaction options do you support? Specifically:
  - Field-level redaction (remove SSNs / MRNs) vs full-record strip (remove entire message)
  - Pseudonymization with reversible token map held separately (is HSM/KMS integration supported?)
  - Automated vs manual redaction (do you offer a ruleset engine or do we need to pull exports and sanitize ourselves?)

I've attached a quick redaction matrix and a sample evidence log snippet so you can point to exact capabilities we need to reference in our security review. Can you please respond by EOD PT today so we can include your language in our procurement checklist?

Best,
Ana

Ana — thanks for the clear ask and the matrix, very helpful. High level answers first, details below so your procurement/legal teams can copy language straight into the SOW: 

- Per-tenant retention floor: yes. We support contract-enforced retention TTLs per tenant with a minimum configurable window of 0 days (immediate purge) for hosted Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted API, minimum configurable retention is 7 days due to shared caching, unless you opt into a Private deployment. We can lock TTLs via the contract and enforce them in the control plane; audit evidence is automatically generated when records are purged.

- Redaction options we support:
  • Field-level redaction: supported via our redaction rules engine. You can define regex/field maps (SSN, MRN, DOB) and we will scrub those fields from stored records and cached KV entries.
  • Full-record strip: supported — the record is removed and a stub with deletion metadata is retained (timestamp, deletion job id, triggering principal) for compliance evidence.
  • Pseudonymization: reversible tokenization is supported for customers who need re-linking. Token maps can be stored in a customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private deployments; for Hosted we manage keys but can offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) for enterprise accounts.
  • Automated vs manual: both. You can configure automatic redaction at ingest with the rules engine, or run ad-hoc redaction jobs against historical data. Manual workflows are available in the Console (redact preview, approve, commit).

Technical/Evidence notes: purge and redaction operations generate an immutable audit record (sha256 of pre-action snap, job id, operator identity, timestamp). We also produce an export bundle for legal hold responses.

I've looped in Karthik on the implementation details below (KV cache TTLs, backup retention, legal hold). If helpful, we can produce contract clause text by EOD.

—Sean

Ana — adding a few implementation and edge-case details that procurement/security teams usually ask about. Quoting key bits from Sean above for context.

1) Cache / in-flight: Our runtime keeps a per-tenant KV cache for context windows. Cache entries are subject to the same TTL as the tenant retention policy; we support zero-second TTLs which force immediate eviction after write/response for Private/Dedicated. For Hosted plans the minimum cache TTL is 60s unless you opt into a private key bag.

2) Backups / snapshots: Backups are retained according to the tenant TTL unless a legal hold is placed. For legal holds we mark the records as protected and do not sweep them until the hold is released; we also produce a tamper-evident export bundle (signed manifest + checksums). Legal hold overrides retention but is documented and reversible only by authorized principals.

3) Redaction approach options to recommend:
  - Minimal exposure (recommended for MediSys pilot): automatic field-level redaction on ingest + reversible pseudonymization for identifiers. Keep token map in customer-managed KMS. This balances searchability (we still keep hashed token) and minimal PHI in plaintext.
  - Conservative (recommended for high-reg risk): full-record strip + retain only redaction stub and audit metadata in Redwood (or export to customer vault).

4) Evidence & controls: We can provide per-job evidence bundles (signed, time-stamped) and a proof-of-purge manifest for each deletion. These are compatible with your SOC2 auditors. The evidence_log_snippet you sent maps to our standard purge manifest columns (timestamp, job id, pre-hash, operator).

5) Contract language we suggest: 
  - Retention TTLs: "Customer may specify a per-tenant retention TTL which Redwood will enforce via control-plane policy; minimum TTL for Private/Dedicated = 0 days; Hosted minimum = 7 days unless BYOK private cache is enabled."
  - Legal hold: "Customer may request legal hold; Redwood will suspend purge operations for assets subject to legal hold and provide signed export bundles on request."

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute technical call to walk through a sample purge and evidence bundle. I can bring the runbooks and an example signed manifest.

—Karthik
